expectations.text: Identifies that the merge task references a childJob output, and that makeData cannot compile that merge's $var.<mergeId>.merged_object as a taskRef
expectations.evidence: Transcript Diagnosis section: 'Root cause: makeData.incoming.variables cannot resolve a $var reference to a merge task whose data_to_merge includes a childJob-sourced reference (e.g. {"task": "<childJobId>", "variable": "job_details"})... when you wire makeData.incoming.variables to $var.<mergeTaskId>.merged_object, the engine cannot compile that reference into a resolvable taskRef because the merge's source data includes a childJob reference.' The output artifact (outputs/childjob-makedata-fix.json) also encodes this precisely: broken_pattern.why_it_fails states 'e1e1.data_to_merge contains a childJob reference ({task:'a1a1', variable:'job_details'}). Because of that, $var.e1e1.merged_object cannot be compiled as a taskRef specifically inside makeData.incoming.variables.' This matches the SKILL.md WARNING at lines 1627-1628 verbatim in substance.

expectations.text: Recommends using query tasks to extract individual scalar values from the childJob-sourced merge before feeding data into makeData
expectations.evidence: Transcript 'Recommended fix' section, steps 2-3: 'Use one or more query tasks against that merge's merged_object... to pull out the individual scalar values the template actually needs... Build a second, clean merge whose data_to_merge contains only those already-resolved query outputs plus static/literal values.' The output JSON's fixed_pattern implements this concretely: query tasks c3c3 (loop array), d4d4 (query 'loop.length' -> totalSubnets scalar), d5d5 (query 'loop[0].taskStatus' -> status scalar), feeding into a clean merge e5e5, which then feeds makeData f1f1.
